_meta.note: Generated from the Cairn app's own field registry, not transcribed. enum = the app REJECTS an off-list value on import. suggest = the app accepts it and warns. optionsFrom: 'data' = the pool is whatever the deck already holds, so there is nothing to check. valueShape: 'array' = a string is an error and is never comma-split; valueShape: 'csv' = a string, and a list is rewritten to a string the first time the card is saved. If your app is newer than the version above, a field here may have moved: check for a newer copy of the skill.

_sections._note: A membership is one of these shapes. A section value outside this list files the card nowhere, silently - matchesSection is exact string equality.
_sections.course_filing: Course cards do NOT use {section: course}: a content card carries {subUnit: <syllabus card id>} and a syllabus card carries {course: <guide id>, unitKey: unit-N}.
_sections.furtherReading_shelf: A work on a principal's shelf carries {cast: <principal id>} ALONE. The app implies Further Reading membership from a cast id beginning fr-member- (matchesSection), and 0 of 2,122 live cards carry both that and {section: furtherReading}.

structural.id: the card's own id - unique in the deck; import replaces a card whole by id
structural.title: the card's name, shown everywhere
structural.memberships: where the card is filed - see sections below
structural.tags: free tags; filters and search read them
structural.source: the reading, course or work this card came from; the string a syllabus resources row's sourceMatch clusters against
structural.track: for research cards, the frontier's title - this is what files the card under its frontier
structural.unit: legacy free-text unit label; empty on every live Field Map card
structural.relatedIds: list of card ids; Related cards render when BOTH cards point at each other

placement_and_structure.sectionRoot: on a guide, the section it heads (cairns | course | fieldMap | research | furtherReading). A frontier card carries sectionRoot: research and a Further Reading principal carries sectionRoot: furtherReading; the registry declares the key on guide only and fixes the value for the other two.
placement_and_structure.courseId: on a courseUnit, the course guide's id
placement_and_structure.order: sort order within a section or unit
placement_and_structure.castMatch: on a Further Reading principal, the cast card's title EXACTLY - this is what pairs the shelf with the person's cast card
placement_and_structure.locations: Field Map: list of sites, each {city, country, latlng, approxLocation, note}
placement_and_structure.latlng: Field Map: card-level coordinates; the map falls back to these when locations[] is absent
placement_and_structure.approxLocation: Field Map: true when the pin is a city-level approximation

declared_or_inert._note: These keys are declared by SOME types and not by others. The app stores whatever you write, and renders the field only on a type that declares it: a maturity badge on a concept card is data with no row on the form and no line on the face. Write them only on the types listed.
declared_or_inert.researchRelevance: concept, cast, framework, library, question, thesis, metric, evidence, institution, platform
declared_or_inert.resourceProgress: no type declares it; it holds the person's own review and flashcard ticks and an assistant never writes it

personal._note: These belong to the person. An assistant leaves them exactly as they are - absent on a new card, untouched on an existing one. The check prints them as NOTES, never as something to fix.

fields.label: Organisation type
fields.help: the kind of organisation it is (lab, funder, nonprofit…). Choose "Other…" to add a type the list does not have yet; it joins the list next time.

fields.label: Organisation type — note
fields.help: why this type was chosen when the organisation does not say so itself, and any part of the old compound description that the sector alone does not carry — an insurer, a media company. orgType is always filled in, so this is where an author judgement is declared instead of being left to look like a stated fact.

fields.label: Geography
fields.help: the countries or regions it mainly operates in. Many values allowed — tap to toggle. Choose "Other…" to add one the list does not have yet; that box alone is comma-separated, so several can be typed at once.

fields.label: Activity bucket
fields.help: what this org or tool mainly does, its category in the Field Map taxonomy. Choose "Other…" to add a category the list does not have yet; it joins the list next time.

fields.label: Frontier(s) touched
fields.help: which research frontier(s) this org or tool touches. Many values allowed — tap to toggle; the "Other…" box alone is comma-separated, so several can be typed at once. This is only the research cross-link; to also show it in a course unit, set that separately in placement.

fields.label: Topics
fields.help: what this organisation is ABOUT — the subject, not the sector or the activity. Many values allowed. Choose "Other…" to add a subject the list does not have yet.

fields.label: City
fields.help: the city it mainly operates from. Leave empty if it has no single base — empty is a legitimate answer here, not a gap.

fields.label: Country
fields.help: the country it mainly operates from. Leave empty if not stated on its own pages.

fields.label: Region
fields.help: the broad region, chosen by hand. Not derived from Country — an organisation with no single country can still be Distributed / global, and an unstated country stays empty rather than being guessed.

fields.label: Safety posture
fields.help: how seriously it treats safety. "none-found" means none found BY US, in the languages we searched, on the pages it publishes — it is a finding. "not-assessed" means we have not looked. Never use one for the other.

fields.label: Safety note
fields.help: one line of evidence for the posture above, in its own terms.

fields.label: Openness
fields.help: what it puts into the commons and whether you can reuse it.

fields.label: Openness note
fields.help: what specifically, and under what licence — open weights, open datasets, CC BY-SA, paywalled, members-only.

fields.label: Work mode
fields.help: how it works across the organisation. A specific role may differ — that is recorded per opportunity.

fields.label: Work mode note
fields.help: the evidence, in its own terms — which roles, which cities, what the page actually states. Leave empty where the mode alone says it.

fields.label: Eligibility
fields.help: constraints that hold across EVERY route it offers — visa sponsorship policy, nationality restrictions, hiring geography. Constraints specific to one route belong on that opportunity, not here.

fields.label: What it argues for
fields.help: One line, in its own terms. Only where the organisation actually takes a position — leave it empty otherwise. Most research bodies do not argue for anything, and an empty stance is a finding rather than a gap.

fields.label: Open opportunities
fields.help: the concrete ways in — one entry per route, each with its own status and dates. Cards still holding the older prose write-up keep it in a plain text box; clearing that box and saving switches the card to the structured editor.

entry.label: Work mode
entry.help: how this specific route works. Resources and collaborations have no work mode — leave them not-stated.
